faq_text: Sources, local models, OCR, and integration with your development tools.
faq_what_answer: Ragmir is the retrieval layer for agentic RAG: it indexes selected project files and returns exact cited passages through TypeScript, CLI, or MCP. Your agent decides when to search again, reasons over the evidence, and generates the answer. Default retrieval works offline without a model download.
faq_private_question: Does Ragmir send my confidential code or documents?
faq_private_answer: Ragmir has no telemetry or hosted document store. It indexes on the machine where it runs and returns unmasked passages. Your chat or agent can forward those passages to a model provider. For confidential work, control the whole path: client, local or self-hosted model, connection, access, and logs. Optional semantic setup explicitly downloads model weights.
faq_agents_question: Which AI agents and tools does Ragmir work with?
faq_agents_answer: Ragmir Core is model-agnostic. Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor install it as a plugin, and Gemini CLI and Qwen Code as an extension, each with the retrieval skill and the MCP server. Kimi, OpenCode, and Cline connect through rgr setup. LangChain.js applications use RagmirRetriever or the agent tools, and Python applications install ragmir, langchain-ragmir for LangChain and LangGraph, or llama-index-retrievers-ragmir from PyPI. Any agent that loads skills installs the Ragmir skills with npx skills add jcode-works/jcode-ragmir, and coding assistants read the documentation on Context7. Other MCP clients, scripts, and CI jobs get the same cited results. Each server reads one project's base and warns or refuses unrelated workspaces.
faq_personal_question: Can I use Ragmir on personal documents, such as bank statements or my CV?
faq_personal_answer: Yes. Index the folders you choose: research and past transcripts for a YouTube script, a lifetime of paperwork, or your whole career history for a job search. Indexing and search run on your machine. Pair Ragmir with a local model such as Ollama to keep every passage there; with Claude Code, Codex, or Claude Desktop, the cited excerpts go to that provider.
faq_team_question: How does a team share the same knowledge base?
faq_team_answer: Commit a shared ragmir.config.json and share reviewed source documents through your normal Git or file-sharing workflow, then run rgr ingest on each workstation, or let rgr hooks install refresh the index after each pull. Each developer keeps a local index. Ragmir does not manage branches or synchronize peers.
faq_offline_question: Does Ragmir require an API key, a model download, or an internet connection?
faq_offline_answer: The default local-hash provider works offline with no API key or model download. Semantic retrieval needs the optional Transformers package and a model preload. A fully local workflow also uses a local consuming model; Ollama is one option. To reuse a model you already serve, the opt-in openai-compatible provider embeds through Ollama, vLLM, or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
faq_observability_question: Can I see where ingestion time and memory are spent?
faq_observability_answer: Optional ingestion metrics report phase timings, throughput, queues, OCR cache hits, and memory use. These local diagnostics omit document content and queries; there is no usage-tracking service.
faq_compare_question: How does Ragmir differ from IDE code indexing or hosted RAG?
faq_compare_answer: Native code search handles structured code well. Ragmir targets project documents that need citations, keeps its index local, and exposes bounded passages through non-destructive MCP tools. Small output budgets keep exact citations and return typed summaries with omission counts.
faq_role_question: Does Ragmir write the answers for me?
faq_role_answer: Ragmir supplies the search and citation tools for agentic RAG. Your agent, chat, or application chooses when to call them and sends the evidence to its model. The integration guide covers local Ollama, self-hosted servers, and cloud providers.
faq_formats_question: Which file formats can Ragmir index?
faq_formats_answer: More than 650 file types index with no extra install: source code in over 200 languages, text, Markdown, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel (macro-enabled files and templates included), OpenDocument, EPUB, HTML and saved web pages, CSV, JSON, YAML, translations, and build files such as Dockerfile. Exports are cited object by object: Figma, Sketch, Excalidraw, and tldraw frames; emails, mailboxes, and Evernote notes; Postman and Insomnia requests; OpenAPI and AsyncAPI operations; PowerDesigner, ERwin, MySQL Workbench, draw.io, Visio, BPMN, ArchiMate, and UML models; Tableau and Power BI projects; GeoJSON features and SARIF findings. Scanned PDFs, photos, and legacy Word files can use optional local extractors, and unsupported files are flagged explicitly.
faq_server_question: Can Ragmir run on a VPS or a server without internet access?
faq_server_answer: Yes. Ragmir runs wherever Node.js 22.12 runs, including Debian and Alpine containers as a non-root user with a read-only filesystem and no network. It opens no HTTP port: agents reach it through stdio MCP, and your service embeds the TypeScript client and owns authentication, authorization, rate limits, and TLS. The official Docker image runs the CLI and MCP server without installing Node.js, and the server guide includes a working Dockerfile.

faq_license_question: Can I ship Ragmir inside a customer deployment or a commercial product?
faq_license_answer: Yes, under the AGPL-3.0 terms, which include offering the source of a modified version you distribute or run for users over a network. To integrate Ragmir into proprietary software or a hosted service without those obligations, JCode Works offers a separate commercial license.
deploy_title: From a customer folder to cited answers, on their infrastructure.
deploy_text: Forward deployed engineers and AI-native teams stand up retrieval where the documents live: a laptop for the first demo, then a VPS, an on-premise server, or a network without internet access.
deploy_item_1_title: A data path you can sign
deploy_item_1_text: Parsing, embeddings, the index, and search run in one Node.js process. No embedding API, telemetry, or hosted store to declare in the security review.
deploy_item_2_text: rgr evaluate scores retrieval on the customer’s own questions, checks exact citations, and counts hard negatives that must return nothing.
deploy_item_3_text: Debian or Alpine containers, a non-root user, a read-only root filesystem, no network. The index lives on a volume and a scheduled job keeps it fresh.
deploy_item_4_text: One committed ragmir.config.json, rgr doctor for diagnosis, and upgrades that keep the last validated index until its replacement passes.
deploy_owns_items: TLS · authentication · per-user access · rate limits · the model
formats_text: More than 650 file types are indexed locally, each with a citation agents can quote. Design files, mail, APIs, data models, and diagrams are cited object by object.
